sections.h2: Is a quick home sale possible in Palm Bay?
sections.html:
Yes. Palm Bay owners can sell to a cash buyer, list with an agent, or sell as-is, and a house needing repairs often suits the first route best. Palm Bay also has an unusual local factor: a November 2026 flood that damaged homes and led the city to change how it handles permits.

The sections below cover the city's growth, its flood and permit rules, and the Brevard County tax steps tied to a sale.

sections.h2: How did Palm Bay grow into Brevard's largest city?
sections.html:
Palm Bay grew mostly in the last half century. The city's history page traces it to the settlement of Tillman at the mouth of Turkey Creek in 1887, renamed Palm Bay in 1925, and incorporated as a city in 1960 with 2,808 residents.

  • U.S. Route 1 opened in 1963.
  • By 1990 Palm Bay had 62,632 residents, the most of any Brevard city.
  • The population passed 100,000 in 2006.
  • Harris Corporation opened a $130 million technology center on Palm Bay Road in 2014.
  • The southern part of the St. Johns Heritage Parkway was finished in 2016, along with plans for a new I-95 interchange in south Palm Bay.

The city also records $13 million in damage and debris cleanup from hurricanes Charley, Frances and Jeanne in 2004. Storm history is a normal part of buyer and insurer conversations here.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Palm Bay?
sections.html:
Palm Bay is a large, moderately priced city by Florida coastal standards. These figures describe the city overall, so use them as background and ask an agent or buyer for a number on your own address.

Source: Census QuickFacts, Palm Bay city. The 2020 density works out to roughly 1,386 people for each square mile, spread thinner than in many neighbors. Veterans number 9,975, and 19.0% of residents are 65 or older.

sections.h2: How did the 2026 flood change selling in Palm Bay?
sections.html:
It added paperwork and, for some owners, financial help. The city's flood page, last updated November 12, 2026, describes road closures, a damage reporting form run by Brevard County Emergency Management, and waived permit fees for residential flood repairs.

  • Fee waiver: the Building Department said it would waive permit fees for flood-related home repairs. Call 321-953-8924 before starting work.
  • Insurance claims: an owner with a National Flood Insurance Program policy needs a substantial damage inspection as part of the claim and before permitting.
  • Disaster Relief Program: the city describes repair help for owners who have lived with a homestead exemption for a year or more, are current on mortgage, taxes and utilities, and have very low or low income. Aid above $20,000 comes as a forgivable 0 percent mortgage over five years.
  • Contractors: the city warns against paying everything upfront and points owners to the state's license lookup.

If your house took on water, an as-is cash sale can spare you a repair project and a permit file. If you repair first, keep photos, estimates and permits together, since a buyer's lender and insurer will ask for them.

sections.h2: What does Palm Bay require for permits?
sections.html:
More than people expect. The city's permit FAQ lists carports, fences, sheds, re-roofing, window and door replacement, air conditioner change-outs, electrical, plumbing, gas work and generators.

Starting without a permit can bring a penalty of up to four times the fees. Residential permits average 14 working days for approval, and applications go through an online portal. An owner-builder permit is allowed only when the property will not be for sale or lease for a year, which matters if you plan to renovate and then sell soon after.

sections.h2: How do Brevard County taxes affect a Palm Bay sale?
sections.html:
The Brevard County Property Appraiser values property each January 1, and bills reach owners in November. The appraiser's site lists a 2026 homestead filing deadline of midnight on Monday, March 2, since March 1 landed on a Sunday that year.

  • The first $25,000 of a homestead exemption reaches all taxes, school taxes included. Up to $25,000 more reduces non-school taxes on value over $50,000.
  • The appraiser's home page carries a notice about Amendment 3 and major homestead exemption changes. Read it before filing.
  • Early payers get 4 percent off in November, falling to 1 percent in February.
  • Bills left unpaid go delinquent on April 1.

sections.h2: What if taxes go unpaid or the owner has died?
sections.html:
A tax certificate sale follows delinquency, and a tax deed can follow later. The collector sells certificates by June 1 to the bidder accepting the lowest interest rate, and a homestead with under $250 owed goes to the county rather than auction. The holder may apply for a deed once two years have passed, and the opening bid on a homestead includes half its latest assessed value. Selling first keeps your equity, since the closing agent pays the delinquent amount from proceeds.

For an estate, summary administration fits non-exempt assets up to $150,000 or a death more than two years back. For a lender case, a show cause hearing comes no sooner than 20 days after the order is served or 45 days after the complaint, and a judicial sale waits at least 20 days after final judgment. Brevard County's Clerk of the Circuit Court keeps these files.

sections.h2: What does a deed cost in Palm Bay?
sections.html: Brevard County charges the state's 70 cents per $100 of price in stamps, collected by the clerk at recording. The title agent lists stamps and recording fees on the settlement statement, so ask for it ahead of closing day.

faqs.q: Are Palm Bay permit fees waived for flood repairs?
faqs.a: The city said it would waive permit fees for residential flood-related repairs after the 2026 flood. Call the Building Department at 321-953-8924 to confirm what applies to your address.

faqs.q: Can I sell a flood-damaged house in Palm Bay?
faqs.a: Yes. Florida does not bar the sale, and an as-is cash sale avoids the repair project. If you have a flood insurance claim, finish the substantial damage inspection first.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for the city's Disaster Relief Program?
faqs.a: The city page lists a one-year ownership requirement, a homestead exemption, current mortgage, tax and utility payments, and very low or low income. Call 321-726-5633 for current details.

faqs.q: What is the deed stamp rate in Brevard County?
faqs.a: 70 cents per $100 of price. Miami-Dade is the only county that differs.

faqs.q: Does my homestead savings pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The next January 1 resets the assessed value to just value. You may carry part of your savings to a new Florida homestead through portability, using form DR-501T within three years.
